The lessons learned from the Ebola Virus Disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo emphasize the importance of early detection, rapid response, and robust infection prevention and control (IPC) measures to mitigate the spread of high-consequence infectious diseases. 2. The use of ultraviolet fluorescence-based simulation has been shown to be an effective method for evaluating the performance of personal protective equipment (PPE) during the initial assessment and care of patients suspected of having high-risk infectious diseases. 3. Compliance with PPE protocols among healthcare workers in high-risk settings can be improved through targeted training and reinforcement of proper donning and doffing techniques, as highlighted in multiple studies. 4. Isolation gowns used in healthcare settings must meet specific fabric and performance standards to ensure adequate protection against infectious agents, as reviewed in the literature. 5. Assessing the PPE needs of healthcare workers is critical to ensuring their safety and the prevention of occupational exposure to infectious diseases, particularly during outbreaks. 6. The performance of isolation gowns has been evaluated to determine their effectiveness in protecting healthcare workers from contamination, with findings emphasizing the need for high-quality materials and design. 7. A highly precautionary doffing sequence for healthcare workers caring for patients with wet Ebola has been proposed to minimize the risk of occupational acquisition of the virus. 8. Interventions such as teamwork training and structured protocols during PPE doffing have been shown to reduce self-contamination among healthcare personnel. 9. The use of fluorescent markers has been demonstrated as a valuable tool for identifying contamination on PPE, aiding in the improvement of donning and doffing practices. 10. Protocol deviations and self-contamination during PPE donning and doffing have been identified as significant risks for healthcare workers, necessitating strict adherence to guidelines and continuous training. 11. Contamination during the removal of PPE by healthcare providers has been documented, underscoring the need for meticulous technique and adherence to established protocols. 12. Human factors risk analyses of PPE doffing protocols for Ebola-level PPE have mapped common errors to contamination risks, providing insights for protocol refinement. 13. Behavioral patterns and faults during PPE doffing for patients with serious communicable diseases have been studied, revealing areas for improvement in training and protocol design. 14. The IPC ring approach, which involves targeted interventions around high-risk healthcare facilities, has shown promise in controlling outbreaks but requires robust IPC training, contact tracing, and triage capacities. 15. Surveillance gaps in Ebola disease monitoring systems have been linked to delayed case detection and response, highlighting the need for comprehensive event-based surveillance systems. 16. Community health monitors and village health teams have played a pivotal role in early case finding, contact tracing, and outbreak containment, demonstrating the value of community mobilization in public health emergencies. 17. Operationally ready isolation centers with geographic and financial accessibility are essential for effective outbreak response, as is the strengthening of medical supply chains to ensure the availability of PPE and other critical resources. 18. A strong and appropriately distributed healthcare workforce, with continuous training in IPC, is critical for managing emerging infectious diseases and ensuring preparedness. 19. Effective communication mechanisms, including risk communication strategies and partnerships with media agencies, are vital for disseminating accurate information and supporting outbreak management efforts. 20. Governance, including leadership and coordination across multiple levels, is a critical enabler of an effective response to emerging infectious disease threats, with the ability to mobilize resources and engage non-state actors being key components. 21. Trust, both interpersonal and institutional, is a foundational element in the relationship between healthcare systems and the communities they serve, influencing the success of public health interventions. 22. The efficacy of various cleaning and disinfection methods, including the use of chlorine solutions and alcohol-based hand rubs, has been evaluated to ensure the inactivation and removal of infectious agents from surfaces and PPE. 23. The impact of multiple alcohol-based hand rub applications on the tensile properties of medical gloves has been studied, emphasizing the need for durable materials in healthcare settings. 24. Contact tracing performance during the Ebola epidemic in Liberia demonstrated the importance of coordinated efforts and the IPC ring approach in identifying and managing cases and contacts. 25. The implementation of the IPC ring approach requires further evaluation to determine its effectiveness in reducing transmission and improving IPC standards in healthcare facilities.
